evidence.positive: Enabled RXNORM_ALLERGY_MAPPING for mgb-mgh only (POST /api/admin/feature-flags/flags, PER_TENANT, enabledTenants=["mgb-mgh"]), then app-launched MGB sample patient MegOne (pmrn 30001024563, case 23151) as loopuser against the live partners.org TST Epic. That patient's AllergyIntolerance list yields patient_allergies row allergen_name=ROCURONIUM, rxnorm_identifier=68139, allergen_id=NULL, reactions=["ANAPHYLAXIS"], severity=MODERATE. After launch, mgb-mgh.patient_medication_allergies gained a medication-level row: allergen_name='Rocuronium', medication_id -> m-rocuronium (the medication_rxnorm_mappings row for rxnorm_code 68139). POST /api/cds/medication-selection/30001024563/23151 with medicationIdentifier=m-rocuronium then returned rule a-general-allergy needsAction=true, ALLERGY_ALLERGEN="Rocuronium", ALLERGY_REACTION="Anaphylaxis", prompt.allowAllergySuppression=true, relevantAllergies[0].rxnormIdentifier="68139"; app log: 'Rule evaluated: a-general-allergy -> true null'. Breadth check on Sallyseventeen (30001007886) produced exactly the mapped set and nothing more: 2180 -> m-cefazolin, 2670 -> m-promethazine-oral, 3423 -> 7 hydromorphone products, 4337 -> m-fentanyl + g-fentanyl-bupivacaine, 7052 -> 3 morphine products.
evidence.negative: Three inverses, all observed at runtime. (1) Shipped default flag state (enabled=false, enabledTenants=[]): same MegOne launch + m-rocuronium selection produced NO medication_id row (only the pre-existing 'Penicillin G Benzathine' -> PENICILLIN category row from the antibiotic path), a-general-allergy was absent from the selection response entirely, and the log read 'Rule evaluated: a-general-allergy -> false patient does not have allergy to the medication'. (2) Tenant scoping: set the flag enabled=true but enabledTenants=["mgb-icsnh"]; the mgb-mgh launch still produced no Rocuronium medication allergy and no alert, so a globally-enabled flag does not leak to an unlisted tenant. (3) No spurious matches with the flag on: AMOXICILLIN (rxnorm 723) and CEFIXIME (rxnorm 25033) have no medication_rxnorm_mappings row and produced no medication-level row (only their antibiotic-path category rows), and PENICILLINS, which arrives with no RxNorm code at all, was skipped by the code filter.
evidence.red_check: Two flips, both reverted. (1) Feature-flag flip: from the shipped default the a-general-allergy alert is absent; flipping RXNORM_ALLERGY_MAPPING on for mgb-mgh made it fire and the log line 'Rule evaluated: a-general-allergy -> true null' appeared (3 occurrences across the run, at 14:08:57, 14:09:35 and 14:18:13, all inside flag-on windows and never while the flag was off or while the pre-fix class was loaded). Flag then reverted to enabled=false / enabledTenants=[] and re-verified: DB row gone, alert gone, feature_flags row byte-identical to the shipped changeset value. (2) Pre-fix class swap: compiled MGBGetPatientInfoStrategy from the merge's parent commit 1fcc3900e inside the container (it differs from HEAD only by the three-line RxNorm branch; lombok 1.18.46 copied in for the @Slf4j/@Getter processing) and dropped the classes into /app/classes, which precedes /app/libs on the jib classpath, then restarted. The app booted cleanly ('Started OrciApplication in 82.758 seconds'). With the flag still ON for mgb-mgh the positive went red: no m-rocuronium row, a-general-allergy absent from the selection response, and the log showed the old FDB path taken instead ('allergen: Rocuronium - type: INGREDIENT - rxnorm: Optional[68139] snomed: Optional.empty' followed by 403 Forbidden from api.fdbcloudconnector.com). Removed the shadow classes, restarted, confirmed /app/classes/com/guided/orci/integration/ is back to its original two Result*.class files and the mgb-client-integration jar md5 is unchanged (0d431ab885858700ee485fd823530d33), and the positive returned (a-general-allergy true / Rocuronium / Anaphylaxis, m-rocuronium row recreated).

caveats: The Mayo half of the change (MayoGetPatientInfoStrategy) was never executed: this instance logs 'Epic OAuth keys not configured - OAuth authentication disabled', so no Mayo patient-info fetch is possible and the Mayo call site was validated only by MGB exercising the same shared method.
FDB returns 403 Forbidden from this instance, so the flag-off fallback was confirmed to be taken (FDB screen request logged) but its real output could not be compared before and after.

Validation exercised the RxNorm-code-to-formulary-medication path this ticket delivers; the shipped AllergyAssociationService on main has since grown SNOMED and cross-reaction-group handling that was not the subject of this run.

The mgb-mgh mapping data maps rxnorm 2670 (codeine) to m-promethazine-oral, so a codeine allergy flags oral promethazine; the code faithfully applies the data but the mapping itself is worth a clinical eyeball.

Relaunching the same case appends duplicate patient_medication_allergies rows rather than replacing them; this affects the pre-existing antibiotic path identically and is not introduced by this change.

automation.assessment: AllergyAssociationServiceTest already covers associateAllergiesViaRxNormMapping and isRxNormMappingEnabled well with mocks (14 cases: no-rxnorm skip, match, no-match, shared code, distinct codes, cross-reaction groups, SNOMED, empty list, and all three flag outcomes). Two gaps are real: the repository query the feature depends on has no test at all, and neither strategy's flag branch is tested, so a future edit could silently point MGB or Mayo at the wrong method with every existing test still green. That branch wiring is exactly what this validation had to exercise by hand.
proposed_tests: orci-repositories: @DataJpaTest for MedicationRxNormMappingRepository.findByRxnormCodeIn covering multi-code IN, the join fetch actually populating medication, and an empty result for an unmapped code.

mgb-client-integration: verify MGBGetPatientInfoStrategy calls associateAllergiesViaRxNormMapping when isRxNormMappingEnabled() is true and associateAllergiesToNonAntibioticAndNarcoticMedication when it is false.
mayo-client-integration: verify MayoGetPatientInfoStrategy calls associateAllergiesViaRxNormMapping when the flag is on and returns an empty list without touching FDB when it is off.
AllergyAssociationServiceTest: add a case asserting an allergy carrying neither an RxNorm nor a SNOMED code short-circuits without hitting either repository.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: With RXNORM_ALLERGY_MAPPING enabled for mgb-mgh, an app launch for a patient whose Epic allergy list carries ROCURONIUM coded rxnorm 68139 created a medication-level allergy against m-rocuronium, and selecting Rocuronium raised the a-general-allergy alert naming Rocuronium and Anaphylaxis.

Negative: With the flag at its shipped default, and again with the flag on but scoped to a different tenant, the same launch and selection produced no medication-level allergy and no alert; RxNorm codes with no formulary mapping produced no match either.

Red check: The flag was flipped on to make the alert fire, then reverted, and separately the pre-fix version of the MGB patient-info strategy was compiled and swapped into the running container, which turned the alert red and sent screening back down the old FDB path before being restored.

Automation: Proposed a repository test for the RxNorm lookup query and strategy-level tests for the feature-flag branch in both the MGB and Mayo patient-info paths.
